findings.title: qid=466 still in priority-queue.json despite popped_by_queue_id=466 on matching review (self-healing on next decider run)
findings.description: Cross-reference between priority-queue.json and curmudgeon/reviews/ found a discrepancy: priority-queue.json[0].queue_id=466 (target=part2, class=deep-attack, pushed 2026-06-03T01:19:36Z) is still present, but the matching review SEC-part2-EXP-450-restructure.c1.json has popped_by_queue_id=466 and popped_by_queue_id_at=2026-06-03T05:16:34.511Z set. The expected sequence (decider.md Step E2): write popped_by_queue_id additively → filter queue → append history to priority-queue-archive.jsonl → fs.writeFileSync priority-queue.json. The first step happened; the latter three did not (priority-queue.json has no commits since ca68cb5; priority-queue-archive.jsonl tail shows qid=460/462/463/465/464 popped but NO qid=466 entry). Possible root causes (low-confidence ordering): (a) decider script aborted between the claimsToWrite loop and the historyAppend.flush + pq write, (b) workspace-sync universal-pusher rescued a stale priority-queue.json from FUSE post-decider-push (priority-queue.json IS in the universal-pusher allow-list per workspace-sync.md), (c) the pop logic was executed in a separate sub-shell that did not have its writes captured. Self-heal: next decider run's pop filter will see qid=466 in queue + matching review with popped_by_queue_id=466 (which IS counted as 'available' by the second clause of the available filter — popped_by_queue_id==null OR popped_by_queue_id===item.queue_id) + strictRev match → shouldPop=true → idempotent claimsToWrite no-op (guard `if(d.popped_by_queue_id==null)`) + queue filter true→remove + archive append for qid=466 → priority-queue.json write. No PROP needed unless this becomes recurring.
evidence: monitor/curmudgeon/priority-queue-archive.jsonl: tail 5 entries are qid 460/462/463/465/464 — qid=466 missing from archive
git log -- monitor/curmudgeon/priority-queue.json: last commit ca68cb5 (the push); no decider-2026-06-03T05-04 (06cae94) touch on this file
findings.counterargument: One could read this as benign: PROP-009r2's strict-match logic IS designed to be idempotent. The next decider run will reconcile. Flagging is over-cautious. Counter-counter: a one-off mutation gap means at minimum the priority-queue-archive.jsonl is missing one event (audit-trail loss), and at worst the next decider run hits a different failure mode and the queue grows. The self-heal claim is theoretical; I have not verified by simulating the next pop.
findings.recommended_action: Watch on next tinker run (~03:30 UTC tomorrow or operator-triggered). If qid=466 is gone AND archive contains a qid=466 entry: confirmed self-heal, close as benign. If qid=466 persists OR a new pop discrepancy appears for a different qid: file a PROP to harden Step E2 (e.g., wrap the historyAppend.flush + pq write in a try/catch with sentinel log, or move them to BEFORE the claimsToWrite flush so partial-write states leave the queue untouched).
findings.verification_pattern: cd /tmp/tinker-clone && node -e "const fs=require('fs');const pq=JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('monitor/curmudgeon/priority-queue.json','utf8'));const stuck=pq.queue.find(q=>q.queue_id===466);const arch=fs.readFileSync('monitor/curmudgeon/priority-queue-archive.jsonl','utf8').split('\n').filter(l=>l.includes('\"queue_id\":466'));console.log(stuck?'STILL_BROKEN — qid=466 still in queue':'FIXED — qid=466 popped');console.log('archive entries for qid=466:',arch.length);"
